newsitem.title: POLAND: Budapest bourse leads East Europe exchanges.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse leads East Europe exchanges.

text.p: The Budapest stock exchange hit new all-time highs this week overshadowing other Eastern European bourses which showed limited price movements in moderate volumes.
Shares in Prague, Warsaw, Bucharest, Bratislava fell while Bulgaria's bourse was flat.
The Central European Share Index (CESI) which measures performance of Prague, Budapest and Warsaw blue-chip stocks fell 0.7 percent to 1,487.15 points.
BUDAPEST
Hungarian stocks hit new highs on Tuesday and Wednesday pushing the BUX index to 3.581.26 but fell on Thursday leaving the bourse little changed from last week's close.
But traders said Thursday's dip was only a profit-taking as investors grew uncertain about the near-term direction, and there were no signs of a reversal of the market's uptrend.
"Day by day the index approached new records or even hit new records so this (uncertainty) can be understood," Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities said.
PRAGUE

Czech shares fell this week in the absence of sufficient demand depressed by concerns about the state of the banking sector after failures of Agrobanka and Kreditni banks and political uncertainty ahead of next month's senatorial polls.
Komercni Banka was the only blue-chip to buck the trend which on Thursday rose 10 crowns to 2,318.
"Komercni is now benefiting from small depositors moving their deposits to bigger banks after the affair with Agrobanka and Kreditini Banka," said Lubomir Vystavel of ING Barings.
Analysts expect big banks in general to benefit from the crisis of smaller institutions as some clients are seen fleeing to the relative safety of large financial institutions.
WARSAW

Polish shares eased this week after moving within a narrow band and analysts expected the market to stay locked in a tight range next week as investors were waiting for clear signals about the bourse's near-term direction.
"The market needs some information to move in either direction, but I don't really know what the information might be," said Pawel Tarnowski of Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
Analysts said the market could stay in the horizontal trend until mid-October when companies' earnings reports for September are due.
BRATISLAVA
Bratislava stocks continued their steady decline this week in light volumes and brokers expected the bearish mood to extend through the end of this year.
Some traders said the 12-share SAX index could soon break the 200 point support.
Leading high-cap issues such as commercial bank IRB, oil refiner Slovnaft and ship-builder Lodenice suffered significant losses.
BUCHAREST
Most share prices sagged under heavy supply on Thursday, when trading reopened after a two-week break to install a new software to improve trading and settlement.
Brokers said investors were waiting for new issues to hit the market and the improved trading system failed to boost volumes.
The bourse said 11 companies had applied for a listing but did not say when they were to join the 13 stocks traded now.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks ended higher on Thursday after trading mixed throughout the week on blue-chip gains and traders expected the bullish mood to prevail for some time.
Istrian hoteliers were the top gainer and traders saw it rising another 20-percent.
Confectioner Kras also continued its steady climb, rising 70 kuna to 620. Fully-listed Pliva fell 150 kuna to 13,000 and Zagrebacka Banka was flat at 1,010 kuna.
BULGARIA

Only one corporate issue traded this week as brokers and investors eyed treasury paper as a more attractive investment after the central bank raised its key interest rate to 300 percent from 108 percent last week, brokers said.
